answer: Behavioral plume tracking. Each identity accrues a private behavioral fingerprint from timing, payload shapes, and interaction graphs. After the fact, a clustering pass detects when many accounts share an unlikely-high overlap—like one operator’s consistent signature. Flagged clusters face retroactive fee clawback and reward forfeiture. To forge distinct fingerprints, an attacker must run each account through separate infrastructure and pacing, multiplying per-identity costs and letting any echo of shared behavior expose the whole set.
